sources.entry: Tapflow - Turn your iPad or Android tablet into a customizable touch control panel for your Mac.

summary.one_liner: Tapflow is a macOS server plus browser-based web editor that turns a tablet or other device's browser into a customizable touch control panel for sending keys, window commands, and audio controls to a Mac.
summary.what_it_does: The Mac runs a Tapflow.app server that receives touch events over WebSocket and injects them into macOS via CGEvent. A tablet or phone opens a URL in its browser on the same WiFi network (port 8082), so no tablet app is required. A web editor lets you drag buttons onto a canvas and set each one's name, color, size, font, and position. The README lists 14 widgets across input (Key, Macro, Text Macro, Touch Pad), audio (Volume, Mic Mute, Audio Out/In), windows (Window Switcher with live thumbnails, Window Click, Window Swipe, Fullscreen), and system (Dock, Switch Profile, Balance for DeepSeek API credit). It also supports multi-select and grouping, undo, and device presets for iPad and Android aspect ratios.
use_cases: Control a Mac from an iPad next to the keyboard
Trigger keyboard shortcuts via on-screen buttons
Switch windows with thumbnails from a tablet
Snap and tile windows with gestures
Start voice input or mute the mic with one tap
Hide the macOS Dock and launch apps from a tablet
how_to_run: Download Tapflow.dmg from Releases and drag it to /Applications
On first open, allow it via System Settings > Privacy & Security > Open Anyway
Grant Accessibility and Screen Recording permissions (Microphone is optional)
Connect the tablet to the same WiFi and open http://<Mac IP>:8082 in a browser
Open the editor on the Mac to customize buttons and save the layout
notable: No app install needed on the tablet; any browser works and supports PWA add-to-home-screen
Window Switcher shows live window thumbnails grouped by app
Window Swipe widget acts as a joystick-style gesture pad for snapping windows
Built-in web editor with drag-and-drop, undo, and grouping
Optional launchd auto-start that relaunches the app after a crash
caveats: macOS only; depends on CGEvent and PyObjC, no Windows or Linux support
The build is signed with a Developer ID but not notarized, so Gatekeeper blocks first launch
Requires Accessibility and Screen Recording permissions; v1 is described as an early test release
